Definition: properly, what leaps forth, i.e. flash of fire, or a burning arrow; also (from the original sense of the root) a bond
BiblicalUsage: Ziyqah is a spark or a flaming arrow — Proverbs pictures a madman throwing firebrands, and Isaiah warns those who light their own sparks that they will lie down in sorrow. The same word also means fetters, the chains that bind prisoners in Psalm 149. Fire and chains: the spark that wounds and the bond that holds.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the two senses belong together — the fires we kindle ourselves end by binding us, and only God's fire sets anyone free.
